summary: Skamania County lookout on a 10-foot wooden tower, registered as built 1938 but shown in 1934 photos; destroyed in 1961, with debris and a rock platform left on the hillside.

facts.design: 10-foot wooden tower with a live-in cab
facts.status_note: Destroyed in 1961. Debris lies down the hillside below the summit, and a rock platform marks where the lookout stood.

access.note: Reached by gravel roads and a short hike of about 0.5 miles with 650 ft of gain, per WillhiteWeb's 2020 route. No closure is described. Level inferred from the route description, not verified with WA DNR.

visit.trail_note: About 0.5 miles and 650 ft of climbing from the ridge west of the peak; in snow, WillhiteWeb hikes up the powerline road instead.

events.note: Panoramic images taken from the roof in July 1934 match the cab on the 10-foot tower; phone line and flagpole already in place.
The register and firelookout.com give 1938; WillhiteWeb says the construction date is not known.
Forest Service told the state DNR it was abandoning Greenleaf and Three Corner Rock. The state planned to rehabilitate it and acquire title.
Benchmark stamped Greenleaf 1946 placed 47.3 feet north northwest of the lookout tower.
Register says removed; firelookout.com says destroyed; WillhiteWeb says the record says destroyed and debris suggests it was pushed down the hillside.

In February 1942, the Forest Service notified the State DNR that they were abandoning Greenleaf and Three Corner Rock lookout houses.
The state quickly responded that they would rehabilitate both and include them in their protective system of lookouts.
Plans were set in motion for the State to procure title for Greenleaf.
In 1946 a benchmark was placed 47.3 feet north northwest of the lookout tower, stamped Greenleaf 1946.
The lookout was said to have been destroyed in 1961.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and firelookout.com give 1938. WillhiteWeb says the construction date is not known and that July 1934 panoramas show the cab. Not resolved; the story gives both.
The register says removed in 1961; firelookout.com and WillhiteWeb say destroyed. WillhiteWeb's December 2019 debris suggests the cab was pushed down the hillside.

notes_for_editor: Build date unresolved: 1938 in the register and firelookout.com, July 1934 panoramas of the cab on WillhiteWeb. Fate and today's state rest on one personal site (2019 visit) plus two register entries. Lead not used: WillhiteWeb links an interview with Gene Sargent, a lookout in summer 1948 at age 16, who mentions hiking to the Three Corner Rock lookout; the page does not clearly state his station, so no staffing claim is made. A replica-cab photo caption on the WillhiteWeb page has no date or place and is not used. The record's agency and county match the sources.
